name: GFP chromophore (HBDI)
description: p-Hydroxybenzylidene-imidazolinone, the Z-isomer that forms inside GFP.

name: GFP (wild-type, 2WUR)
description: Aequorea victoria GFP, 0.9 Å X-ray structure. Abs 395/475 / Em 509 nm.

name: EGFP (2Y0G)
description: Enhanced GFP (F64L/S65T). Abs 488 / Em 507 nm. The standard green FP.

name: mCherry (2H5Q)
description: Monomeric red FP derived from DsRed. Abs 587 / Em 610 nm.

name: JF525
description: Janelia Fluor 525 on its own: a rhodamine with two 3,3-difluoroazetidines. The free acid; linkers attach at the spare carboxyl. Abs 525 / Em 549 nm.

name: JF525 HaloTag ligand
description: Janelia Fluor 525: a rhodamine with two 3,3-difluoroazetidines, plus the chloroalkane linker that HaloTag grabs. Abs 525 / Em 549 nm.

name: HaloTag7 (6Y7A)
description: Engineered bacterial dehalogenase, 293 residues, 1.40 Å X-ray structure. Asp106 at the bottom of its tunnel attacks the ligand's chloroalkane. Protein only.

name: HaloTag7–JF525
description: JF525 bonded to Asp106; the chloride has left. Model: the TMR dye in 6Y7A with its amino groups changed to difluoroazetidines. The dye starts lit so you can find it.

name: Acetabularia rhodopsin (3AM6)
description: Seven-helix proton pump from a green alga, 3.20 Å X-ray structure. Retinal sits in the middle, bonded to Lys211. Parent of the voltage sensor in Voltron. The retinal starts lit.

name: Voltron525 (model)
description: Ace2N rhodopsin fused straight to HaloTag7 carrying JF525: five residues removed, no linker. Membrane voltage shifts the retinal's absorption, which quenches the dye by FRET. Composite: the pose of the two domains is modelled.

name: Ace2N-mNeon (model)
description: The same rhodopsin fused to the fluorescent protein mNeonGreen, a GFP-like barrel, and Voltron's predecessor. Composite: the pose of the two domains is modelled.

name: Voltron525 in a membrane (model)
description: Voltron525 set into a POPC bilayer, seen side on: cytoplasm below, outside above. The lipids are a frame from a published simulation, drawn faint; nothing was relaxed around the protein.
